27616123.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27616123.value: 信托法控制受托人自由裁量权的议题非常复杂和困难。在香港、澳大利亚和英国，法律在这方面的发展尚存在很多不足。通过应用基于自治的自由主义理论，本项目将研究这些地区明示私人信托中信托法控制受托人自由裁量权的方式。该项目主要关注受托人在信托事务管理和信托财产处理方面获得自由裁量权的情形。根据所涉及的权力条款，不同信托中受托人对信托事务管理的自由裁量权可能存在很大差异。然而，无论自由裁量权的程度和范围如何，受托人行使自由裁量权都受到各种有意义的限制，例如严格的诚实信用义务、合理谨慎义务以及仅考虑受益人利益的义务。这些限制旨在减少受托人滥用自由裁量权的风险，从而最大程度上地保护受益人利益。这些限制如何和在多大程度上指导受托人行使权力，对于决定信托设立人是否愿意利用信托工具执行其财产计划，以及受益人在信托管理中的利益是否能够得到公平保护具有重要影响。本项目的假设是，在以自治为基础的自由主义理论框架下，信托法的最终目标是在保护每一方自治利益的基础上，促进信托活动所涉及的所有当事人总体自治利益的最大化。这些当事人包括设立人、受托人、受益人和与受托人交易的第三方。基于这个假设，需要探讨的核心问题是：一个有效的控制受托人自由裁量权的框架应该是什么样子的？本项目采用的方法包括理论研究、法教义学探讨和比较法分析。本项目预期的成果是在国际领先期刊上发表两篇文章。

27616423.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27616423.value: This study investigates urban solutions that confront the compounding effects of environmental risks and sociopolitical divides for planetary sustainability. It is founded on three propositions originating in my former research: 1) the meanings of climate adaptation and social-environmental justice vary across scales, classes, cultures, and sociopolitical systems; 2) solutions for planetary sustainability must move beyond universalist and technocratic approaches by embracing cultural sensitivity, engaging local networks, and buildings bridges across communities and borders; and 3) city design and development is crucial to intertwined socio-environmental transitions towards sustainable futures. Accordingly, I investigate ideas and practices that aim at ecological restoration and climate adaptation in post-industrial societies in search of barriers to, and accelerant factors for, progress. I ask: Who has the power to shape ecological visions of urban futures? How do these actors operationalize their idea(l)s and where do they find inspiration? In turn, in what ways does implementing ecological design influence local society and urban practice during post-industrial transitions? I propose a three-year study that will utilize available data, expert interviews, and field research to: 1) create a global atlas to analyze and compare salient typologies of restorative and adaptive practices with top-down and/or bottom-up approaches; 2) assess focused cases in Asia to reveal these practices’ socio-environmental outcomes and underlying policy mobilities; and 3) discuss inherent power dynamics that hinder/accelerate meaningful and just solutions for socio-environmental sustainability. While background cases are drawn globally to enable cross-border comparisons, focused case studies will prioritize Asian cities influenced by colonialism and neoliberal globalization to reveal intra-Asia and/or West-East/North-South policy mobilities. As scholarship on Asia’s “eco,” “green,” and “sustainable” cities has provided vital critiques highlighting past failures, this research promotes “hopeful epistemologies” in political ecology and aims to nudge the discourse beyond the existing “systemic revolution or nothing” disposition. The research aims at four contributions: 1) to examine variegated solutions to planetary issues with cosmopolitan, comparative, and relational approaches; 2) to draw insights beyond finding fault per se and start identifying practical pathways and incremental changes towards hopeful transitions; 3) to foreground Asia as a key site of knowledge production, (re)invention, and export to complement long-standing, Western-derived understandings of the modern city; and 4) to connect scholarship with action and education through practice-oriented research and community-based fieldwork. This study will involve students and experts from diverse backgrounds to enable project-based, intercultural learning and bring together scholars, practitioners, community members, and policy-makers through international conference(s). 27616923.value: 情感安全的跨語言空間對於支持香港少數族裔學生管理第二語言課堂焦慮的作用：漢語作為附加語言課堂的研究

27616923.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
27616923.value: 第二語言課堂焦慮是在課堂上學習或使用第二語言時的情感反應。它與一系列複雜的語言劣等情結有關，包括對第二語言學習和使用在課堂上感到尷尬和缺乏自信的感覺。香港的少數族裔學生在學習中文作為第二語言方面遇到了困難，而中文教學的不足往往被認為是移民家庭社會流動性和代際貧困受限的原因。少數族裔學生在學校學習中文所面臨的語言挑戰可能是他們焦慮的來源，這可能會阻止他們融入香港社會。 然而，關於教師如何創建積極的課堂氛圍以減輕學生的L2課堂焦慮的研究尚缺乏。本研究提出了一種混合方法和多地點的方法，並採用跨語言實踐（translanguaging）作為分析視角。跨語言實踐是指讓老師和學生全面運用語言，以及不同的溝通模式以建構意思。本研究旨在調查如何創建情感安全的跨語言空間來減輕少數族裔學生在學習中文作為第二語言時的焦慮。 在量化方面，本研究將使用問卷來確定少數族裔學生的中文作為第二語言課堂焦慮水平。半結構化訪談，錄像課堂互動和錄像刺激回憶訪談將提供有關以下方面的質性見解：（1）少數族裔學生與焦慮相關的個人和情境因素以及他們在學習中文作為第二語言時如何體驗焦慮，（2）教師如何建立跨語言空間以最大限度地減少學生的中文作為第二語言學習焦慮，以及（3）教師和學生如何理解中文作為第二語言課堂中的跨語言實踐。課堂互動數據將使用多模式會話分析進行分析。然後，將與錄像刺激回憶訪談進行三角測量，將解釋現象學分析應用於調查教師和學生對中文作為第二語言課堂中跨語言實踐的反思。研究結果將提供重要見解，以了解學生在跨語言空間中的體驗，旨在為中文作為第二語言學習創建積極的課堂氛圍。這些見解將允許發展可持續的教學方法，以供預培訓和在職教師使用，讓他們利用學生豐富的語言和文化知識來減輕他們的中文作為第二語言學習焦慮。

28604023.label: Project Title(Chinese)
28604023.value: 藏緬語中橋接重複的類型學研究

28604023.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
28604023.value: Bridging repetition, or tail-head linkage, is a common spoken phenomenon in procedural description and folklore narration of many lesser-known languages of the world. Its core feature is that an element of one clause, generally involving the predicate, is repeated verbatim in the following clause. Its pervasive use in continuous event line exhibits the pattern of [(A,) B]sentence 1[B, C]sentence 2[C, D]sentence 3[...]sentence n. The repetition maintains the cohesion of oral discourse. Although this sentence-linking phenomenon is extremely repetitive and stylistically unusual in well-known languages, such as English, it is used frequently and also relatively well-studied in languages of Papua New Guinea and Amazon. While this oral phenomenon also exists widely in Tibeto-Burman languages, such as Japhug rGyalrong, Puxi Qiang, and Ersu, in Yunnan and Sichuan, China, it has seldom been the subject of any substantial studies within Tibeto-Burman linguistics. Therefore, firstly, the present study generalizes the morphosyntactic and discourse characteristics of bridging repetition in Tibeto-Burman languages by analyzing the procedural descriptions and folklore narrations of 7 selected Tibeto-Burman languages. Part of the data were collected first-hand through fieldwork and the rest taken from endangered language digital archives (e.g., Pangloss and ELAR). Moreover, an investigation into Tibeto-Burman languages is likely to pinpoint the morphosyntactic characteristics that bridging repetitions correlate with, such as zero anaphora. This is a question which has not been satisfactorily solved since de Vries (2005). Finally, the PI hypothesizes that the morphosyntactic conditions must combine with a non-grammatical condition, namely the target language lacks a practical writing system, so as to function as the sufficient and necessary conditions for the occurrence of bridging repetition. Such languages have not been touched by literacy or any knowledge of writing and print, and are used only in spoken domains. A culture with such a language is called primary orality (Ong 1982). Bridging repetition is utilized in primary orality, not only as a cohesive device, but also an important cognitive device and an artful means to reduce the workload of information processing for both narrators and hearers under the changing oral context. Therefore, to test this hypothesis, bridging repetition of the Tibeto-Burman languages, as well as that in the existing literature, is further compared with at least 11 other languages (e.g., English, Beijing Mandarin, Nepali) which have well-established writing systems. 橋接重複存在於世界上諸多語言的口語敘述中，如口述程式和口述故事等。橋接重複也被稱為尾首連接，是一種連接句子的手段，它的核心特點是相鄰兩個子句的謂語相互重複，主要功能是促成句間連貫、推進故事事件的發展。在口語敘述中，連續使用橋接重複會呈現以下現象：[A, B]句子1[B, C]句子2[C, D]句子3[...]句子n。橋接重複在許多知名語言中並不多見，如英語等，但在亞馬遜和巴布新幾內亞的語言中則非常常見。橋接重複也普遍存在于諸多藏緬語中，如在中國四川和雲南等地使用的嘉絨語、普米語、羌語、爾蘇語等。但是，目前文獻中少有有關藏緬語橋接重複的研究。因此，本研究選取了7種藏緬語，通過分析非經編輯的口述程式和口述故事，歸納藏緬語中橋接重複的形態句法特點和語篇特點。數據來源分為兩部分：一部分是田野調查的一手資料，另一部分是瀕危語言的數位檔案資料，如Pangloss和ELAR。另外，本研究旨在解釋橋接重複的出現原因，如語言中的零回指特徵。另一個導致橋接重複頻繁出現的可能原因是：某些語言沒有書寫系統。這些語言社會以口語文化為主，不同於依賴文字和印刷的主流語言社會（如漢語和英語社會），其社會文化和經驗一般依靠口頭傳承，沒有被大眾掌握的民族文字。這樣的語言社會被稱為原發口傳社會（Ong 1982）。因此，本研究假設，橋接重複在原發口傳社會中不僅銜接故事發展，還是一種緩解信息處理壓力的重要手段；在不斷變化的口語環境中，敘述者利用橋接重複這種巧妙的連接方法，幫助自己和聽者處理信息。為驗證假設，本研究將對比有書寫系統的語言使用橋接重複的情況，如英語，北京官話等。

28604623.label: Project Title(Chinese)
28604623.value: 同步線上數學教學的設計與實踐：可視化學習分析支持下的設計為本研究

28604623.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
28604623.value: After prolonged face-to-face class suspension in Hong Kong, synchronous online instruction―a fallback teaching approach during the COVID-19 pandemic―is currently used to provide after-school support for students lagging behind in mathematics. However, ensuring student learning and engagement in online lessons is challenging. Teachers also lack the knowledge and skills to engage students in problem solving and online class discussion. To address these challenges, we first propose improving the design and practice of synchronous online mathematics instruction using (1) variation theory which can guide designing a series of problems and teachers’ mathematical discourse to facilitate students’ online learning and (2) academic productive talk which can inform how teachers engage students in online class discussion. Second, we propose supporting teacher improvement using our visual learning analytics (VLA) approach. Leveraging a set of visualization principles of VLA strategies (e.g., multiple visualization), the approach will be refined to analyze and visualize online lesson video data which can facilitate teacher reflection. With this theoretical foundation, we will conduct a two-year design-based study involving 10 secondary schools. As many schools give priority to students lagging behind, we will develop a 16-lesson supplementary program covering a series of essential foundation topics in Hong Kong secondary mathematics curriculum. In each school, two to four teachers, each of whom teaches the program three times across three semesters, will participate in the study with their Grades 11–12 students (i.e., about 30 teachers and a total of 1,350 students). Both quantitative (analytics from lesson videos, student survey, and student achievement tests) and qualitative (lesson video content, teacher reflection records, and participant interviews) data will be collected and analyzed via the mixed methods approach. This study has four design phases: (1) identify problems via small-scale interventions by analyzing lesson videos and participant interviews (e.g., decreased student responsiveness to questions); (2) develop initial solutions to the problems (e.g., using an “explain other” talk move to invite specific students in class discussion); (3) evaluate and refine the outcomes of Phase 2 through three one-semester iterations by analyzing teachers’ discourse practice, students’ engagement in class discussion, their mathematics achievement, participants’ perceptions, and their suggestions. The findings from each iteration will inform the interventions in the next one; and (4) conduct overall reflection. We expect this study will contribute to generating design principles that teachers can use in synchronous online mathematics instruction and a VLA-supported approach that helps them review and improve their teaching practice. 香港經歷了長期的暫停面授課堂，同步線上教學成為COVID-19疫情期間的替代教學方法，目前仍用於為數學成績稍遜的學生提供課後支援。然而，確保學生在線上課堂中的學習和參與卻具挑戰性。教師也缺乏引導學生進行解難和線上課堂討論的知識和技巧。 為應對這些挑戰，我們首先提出改善同步線上數學教學的設計與實踐，運用 (1) 變易理論來設計一系列問題和教師的數學對話，以促進學生的線上學習，及 (2) 有效學術性對話來指導教師如何引導學生參與線上課堂討論。另外，我們提出運用我們的可視化學習分析（VLA）方法來支持教師的改進。我們將利用VLA策略的可視化原則（例如：多重視像化）改良我們的VLA方法，以分析和視像化線上課堂錄影的數據，從而促進教師的反思。 有了這個理論基礎，我們將進行為期兩年的設計為本研究，涉及10所中學。由於許多學校均著力幫助成績稍遜的學生，我們將設計一個16課時的提升課程，涵蓋香港中學數學課程中的基礎課題。在每所學校，2至4位教師將在三個學期內舉辦三次課程，給予他們的中五和中六學生（即約30位教師和1350名學生參與研究）。我們將透過混合研究方法進行數據收集和分析，包括量性數據（課堂錄影分析、學生調查和學生成績測試）和質性數據（課堂錄影內容、教師反思記錄和參與者訪談）。 本研究包含四個設計階段：(1) 通過分析課堂錄影和參與者訪談來識別問題（例如：學生對提問的反應減少）；(2) 制定解決問題的初步方案（例如：運用「解釋他人」對話方式邀請特定學生參與課堂討論）；(3) 通過三次一個學期的循環來評估和改進第2階段的成果，評估教師的對話實踐、學生在課堂討論中的參與、數學成績、參與者的觀感和建議。每個循環的研究結果將指導下一階段的實踐策略；(4) 進行整體性的反思。 我們期望這項研究能總結出教師在同步線上數學教學中可以使用的設計原則，以及一個VLA方法來幫助教師檢視和改進他們的教學實踐。

28606923.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
28606923.value: 在香港，關於精神健康的公眾和專業知識、理念與實踐都在歷史上受到不同的認識論、文化與意識形態的影響。在過去的幾年裡，香港本地的公眾精神健康宣傳活動持續增加。這些活動旨在減少本地大眾精神健康意識及知識的持續匱乏並應對社會內日益增長的精神健康問題。然而，我們還未能知曉這些公眾活動推廣的對於精神健康的認識論、文化和意識形態視角在這個複雜的社會環境下是否促進共融及賦權。為了調查這個問題，此青年學者計劃項目將採用批判多模態語篇分析法來解析現時香港公眾精神健康宣傳活動的傳意、認識論、文化與意識形態方面的特徵。 該項目專注於完成三項任務。第一項任務是展示和比較這些公眾宣傳活動如何通過不同的傳意行為和話語材料推廣關於精神健康的不同知識、理念與實踐體系。第二項任務是對這些被推廣體系的認識論、文化及意識形態層面進行批判性檢驗並指出這些體系相應的在香港社會環境內的優點與缺點。基於整個研究項目的結果，最後一項任務是揭示以及評判現時香港的公眾精神健康宣傳活動在傳意、認識論、文化與意識形態層面的主要特點。該項目主要會蒐集四類數據資料：(i) 宣傳活動中使用的主要話語材料（‘中心話語材料’），(ii)對宣傳活動的觀察記錄，（iii）其他影響中心話語材料內容與設計的現有信息，（iv）半結構性訪談。另外，此項目會採用批判性多模態語篇分析法來揭示與評判這些公眾宣傳活動所推廣的對於精神健康的認識論、文化及意識形態視角。 該項目相信將對相關的學術、教育、職業與政策產生顯著影響。一方面，其會從文化與批判視角來豐富我們對於精神健康與精神健康信息溝通的理論認識，從而可以促進現有和未來相關課題的學術與教育活動。另外一方面，該項目的成果可以幫助香港本地及其他地區的精神健康組織和相關人士評估和提升他們現有的公眾和專業知識、實踐與政策。

28609623.label: Project Title(Chinese)
28609623.value: 遊戲中學習相等概念：與兒童和照顧者一起設計、測試和分析遊戲

28609623.label: Abstract as per original application (English/Chinese)
28609623.value: Early math performance has substantial long-term impacts on children’s achievement and life outcomes, yet few resources are available for math learning in early childhood within and beyond Hong Kong. The lack of developmentally appropriate resources has led educators to adapt primary school instruction for preschoolers, negatively impacting children’s later achievement. To address this urgent need, we will work with stakeholders to design, test, and analyze math learning through a game. The game will leverage action and perception to support learning of math concepts (i.e., equivalence), language (e.g., more, after, between), and relations between numbers (e.g., 3 is less than 4). We focus on these knowledge and skills because they have lasting impacts on important outcomes, such as general math achievement and abstract reasoning. First, we will work with children, parents, and teachers to design a game and in-game support for language and numerical skills using readily accessible play materials. Second, we will conduct an experiment to examine the effects of various in-game support on math learning. Specifically, kindergartners will play the game for four 20-minute sessions in one of four conditions that includes support for language only, number only, both, or neither (i.e., free play control). We will measure children’s math concepts, language knowledge, and numerical skills before and after the play sessions to quantitatively examine the effects of different support on these aspects of knowledge and skills. Third, we will work closely with caregivers to qualitatively analyze children’s learning behaviors during game play. We aim to identify the mechanisms through which language and numerical skills support learning of math concepts. This research is significant and innovative in several ways. By involving stakeholders in the design process, we will design a game that is engaging, feasible, and culturally relevant for children, parents, and teachers to use in home and classroom environments. This participatory design work will also inform future research and development of games that support playful learning. The findings from the experiment will reveal whether language and numerical skills support learning of math concepts. Delineating the learning mechanisms will inform theories of math development and provide curricular implications on appropriate sequences of instruction. Finally, by working with stakeholders on the interpretation of data, the project will provide practical insights into learning and ways to support it among young children across everyday contexts. Ultimately, this work will contribute to theories and practices for early math learning. 早期數學表現對兒童未來成就和生活具有重大的長期影響，但香港內外可用於幼兒時期數學學習的資源很少。 由於缺乏適合幼兒發展的學習資源，教育工作者不得不使用小學教材來教導學齡前兒童，這對兒童後來的成績產生負面影響。 為了解決這一迫切需求，我們將與兒童、家長和老師合作，一起設計、測試和分析遊戲中學習數學的過程。 該遊戲將利用行動和感知來支持數學概念（即相等概念）、語言（例如，更多、之後、之間）以及數字之間的關係（例如，3 小於 4）的學習。 我們關注這些知識和技能，因為它們對兒童認知發展具有久遠影響，例如：數學成績和抽象推理。 首先，我們將與兒童、家長和教師合作，使用易於獲取的遊戲材料，設計遊戲並在遊戲中支持語言和數字技能。 其次，我們將進行一項實驗來檢測各種遊戲內支持對數學學習的影響。 具體來說，幼兒園兒童將被分為四組，每組皆玩四次 20 分鐘的遊戲。其中一組的遊戲僅支持語言、一組僅支持數字、一組兩者都支持和一組兩者都不支持（即自由遊戲）。 我們將在遊戲前後測量孩子的數學概念、語言知識和數字技能，以檢測不同遊戲對這些知識和技能方面的影響。 第三，我們將與家長及教師密切合作，定性分析孩子在遊戲過程中的學習行為。 我們的目標為了解語言和數字的技能是如何支持數學概念的學習。 這項研究在幾個方面都具有重要意義和創新性。 通過讓師生家長參與設計過程，我們將設計一款引人入勝、可行且與在地文化相關的遊戲，供兒童、家長和教師在家庭和課堂環境中使用。 這項參與式設計將為未來支持寓教於樂的遊戲、研究和開發提供信息。 實驗結果將揭示語言和數字技能是否支持數學概念的學習。 描述學習機制將為數學發展理論提供信息，並為適當的教學順序提供課程建議。 最後，通過與家長和老師合作解釋與分析數據，該項目將提供有關學習的實用見解以及在日常環境中支持幼兒學習的方法。 最終，這項工作將為早期數學學習的理論和實踐做出貢獻。
